paragraphs.zh: Reference throughout this specification to “one embodiment” or “an embodiment” means that a particular feature, structure or characteristic described in connection with the embodiment is included in at least one embodiment. Thus, the appearances of the phrases “in one embodiment” or “in an embodiment” in various places throughout this specification are not necessarily all referring to the same embodiment. Furthermore, the particular features, structures, or characteristics may be combined in any suitable manner in one or more embodiments.

paragraphs.zh: In some embodiments, the numbers expressing quantities of ingredients, properties such as concentration, reaction conditions, and so forth, used to describe and claim certain embodiments of the invention are to be understood as being modified in some instances by the term “about.”  The term “about” may refer to ± 5 of the specific figure preceding the term “about”. In some embodiments, the numerical parameters should be construed in light of the number of reported significant digits and by applying ordinary rounding techniques. paragraphs.notes: Marker printed as four digits. Twelve printed lines. The plus-minus is printed as a plus glyph with a separate horizontal bar beneath it, typewriter fashion, with a space before the 5: read as U+00B1 and transcribed '± 5'. This is the one character on the page I am not fully certain of; a reader wanting the literal glyph should see the page. Note the patent gives no unit and no percent sign after the 5, so 'may refer to ± 5 of the specific figure' is what is printed and nothing has been supplied. Quoting of 'about' is inconsistent and kept so: '“about.”' has the period inside the quote, '“about”.' has it outside, one line apart. 'Not withstanding' is printed as two words; magnified and confirmed, kept verbatim. Three measured double spaces after sentence periods, each roughly twice the median word gap on its own line: after '“about.”', after 'a particular embodiment.' and after 'ordinary rounding techniques.'. The gap after '“about”.' measures the same as an ordinary word gap and is a single space. Left margin line numbers 20 and 25 excluded.
